description: Authored lesson sequences for district-paced units whose membership is an INSTRUCTIONAL DECISION rather than the curriculum's own unit numbering, plus the declared disposition of every canonical lesson the resulting plan does not schedule exactly once. Hand-maintained and reviewed. Everything not listed here falls back to the curriculum manifest's unit membership, in manifest order.
note: Lesson ids ONLY. Titles, standards and routes resolve from data/curriculum-launch-manifest.json at render time, so a lesson renamed in the curriculum is renamed everywhere. Listing a lesson here does NOT move it: 2-6 remains canonically a Unit 2 lesson and still appears in Unit 2's own list.

PRE.reason: The Pre-Unit is assembled, not inherited. It is a prerequisite-fluency sequence drawn from several canonical units to rebuild what Course 1 assumes — whole-number, decimal and fraction division before ratio reasoning starts in Unit 3. Reading its membership off the curriculum's unit-1 numbering produced 1-1 through 1-6, which is a different thing: the Unit 1 'Math Is…' arc, not the review the district actually paces here.

dispositionNote: An assembled unit occupies a slot in the district plan, so the plan no longer schedules every canonical lesson exactly once. Both directions of that are declared here rather than tolerated: a lesson the plan never schedules, and a lesson it schedules more than once. validate:pacing-unit-order asserts this list against the dated plan in BOTH directions — an undeclared omission fails, an undeclared repeat fails, and a declaration whose lesson no longer matches its declared occurrences fails too, so this file cannot decay into stale absolutions. `reviewStatus` is 'confirmed' only where a source document settles it; anything resting on a teaching judgement is 'teacher-review' and is expected to stay that way until a human answers the question in `openQuestion`.

lessonDispositions.reason: Unit 1's 'Math Is…' arc is not paced this year. The district workbook contains no Unit 1 row at all: its eleven units are Pre-Unit, 3, 4, 6, 7, 8, 9, 5, 2, MSTAR, 10. The Pre-Unit stands in that slot, and the confirmed Pre-Unit sequence keeps only 1-1 from the arc as the opening community lesson. Unit 10 ('Math Is...', 10-1 … 10-6) revisits the same arc at the end of the year.

surplusDay.reason: Not a judgement call — the generator's own documented rule. The Pre-Unit's 11 slots hold 5 lessons + Review + Assessment + 2 project days = 9, leaving 2 surplus. Assumption #14 spends the first on a second day for the opening lesson (1-1, Aug 24–25). Assumption #7 spends the next on a catch-up ANCHOR, taken in lesson order, and the first Pre-Unit lesson that owns a catch-up surface is 2-7. The station it opens is titled '2.6 · 2.7 · 2.11 · 2.12 Catch-Up', so it repairs exactly the two division-algorithm lessons taught immediately before it.
evidence: docs/pacing-sources/build/plan_core.py — build_items(): `anchors = [l['id'] for l in ls if l['id'] in cu]`, then `use_cu = set(anchors[:surplus])`

culminatingProject.reason: Audited rather than renamed, and it is the right project. The page at /math/unit-1/projects/ is titled 'Number Sense in Action' and describes itself as 'greatest common factor, least common multiple, decimal operations, and multi-digit division', citing 6.NOS.2, 6.NOS.3 and 6.NOS.4. That is the Pre-Unit's own mathematics — 2-6 is 6.NOS.2 and 2-7 is 6.NOS.3 — and it is NOT the 'Math Is…' arc, whose lessons carry MPP.3 and grade-5 standards. The project fits the corrected Pre-Unit better than it ever fitted the inferred one. It keeps its canonical name because the manifest generates 'Unit N Culminating Project' uniformly for all ten units; special-casing one would put a second name for the same surface into circulation, which is the class of problem this whole file exists to prevent.
